text: Age: 36
Occupation: Teacher/Governing Board Member

Since 2021, I've had the honor of serving on the Lynwood Unified School District Governing Board of Education. My colleagues appointed me to join them in service, and in 2022 I won election to a four-year term unopposed. This year I ask for your vote to continue serving Lynwood students and families on the Lynwood School Board.
Since joining the board, I've tirelessly advocated for resources and improvements that benefit students:

- lobbying for funding to rebuild Lynwood High School on Imperial Highway
- championing recognition and support for our most vulnerable and marginalized students and families
- demanding improved classrooms and facilities.

One of my earliest priorities was renovating our athletic facilities; today a Sports Complex is underway, including a refurbished football field, a new baseball field, a new softball field, and a multipurpose field.

I believe in teamwork and measurable results. My experience playing youth baseball and soccer, combined with my work as a Restorative Justice teacher, informs my collaborative leadership and commitment to safe, supportive schools where every student can thrive. Together we can promote rigorous college and career pathways, restorative justice practices for accountability and healing, and stronger parent involvement. Vote for
on November 3rd.

text: Occupation: Educator/Coach

James Bishop, for the past 45 years, I have proudly called Lynwood home. During that time, I have dedicated more than 35 years of service to the Lynwood Unified School District as a Safety Officer, Coach, and Vocational Education Teacher.

I have had the privilege of working with students, families, teachers, and staff from every corner of our community. I understand the challenges, opportunities, and strengths that make our community special. I understand the needs of our students, the concerns of our teachers, and the expectations of our families. I have seen firsthand how decisions made at the district level impact the people we serve every day. My commitment will be to advocate for what is best for students, educators, and strengthen the connection between our schools and the community.

I believe effective leadership starts with listening, understanding, and being present. My roots in Lynwood run deep! My experience comes from decades of working side-by-side with the people who make this community great.
If elected, I will be a strong voice for students, teachers, employees, and families, always putting the needs of our community first!

Together, we can build a stronger future for Lynwood.
— James Bishop Sr.
Candidate for Lynwood Unified School District Board of Education

text: Age: 49
Occupation: Business Owner
I am running for the Lynwood Unified School District Board to put students first, strengthen parent involvement, and bring greater accountability to our schools.

As a longtime Lynwood resident, business owner, Planning Commissioner, former PTO President, and former DELAC President, I have spent many years serving our community. I have served for over 15 years as a parent and President of the Lynwood Marlins Swim Team, and I currently serve as Vice President of the Lynwood Sports Association (LSA).
I understand the importance of creating safe schools, supporting teachers, improving academic achievement, and preparing students for college, careers, and a successful future.
I will listen to parents, ask tough questions, protect taxpayer dollars, and work to ensure district decisions are transparent and focused on students.
Our children deserve strong schools, responsible leadership, and every opportunity to succeed.
I respectfully ask for your vote.

text: Occupation: School Community Liaison

I am Mariela Renteria, born and raised in Lynwood and a proud product of Lynwood Schools. Lynwood gave me so much, and I've spent my career finding ways to give back. For the last three years, I've worked in a neighboring community helping schools and families connect and support one another. This work has shown me exactly how school systems function, where they fall short, and what it takes to fix them.

That understanding started early. As a high school student here, Lynwood alumni mentored me and taught me the value of community service. I went on to pursue my degree at UC Riverside, and everything I've learned since has been in service of one goal: making sure Lynwood families have the resources and access they deserve.

I know how school systems work from the inside — the policies, the budgets, the barriers families face — better than most. Now I'm ready to bring that knowledge home, to serve Lynwood the way it once served me.
Mariela Renteria: For Lynwood. For our students. For our future.

text: Occupation: Mother/Community Organizer

My name is Martina Rodriguez. As a proud Lynwood resident and homeowner for over four decades, my commitment to our city and its schools runs deep. Three of my four children are graduates of the Lynwood Unified School District, and my youngest is now a freshman at Lynwood High School.

I previously served as an LUSD Board Member from 2001 to 2005, and my mission hasn't changed. As a community organizer, I have spent two decades showing up at every board meeting, working with families from the outside to cut through bureaucracy, and carrying our community's voice into rooms where decisions get made.

Our district faces real challenges today, and our children deserve leadership that meets this moment head-on. I am running for LUSD Governing Board Member again to make sure our district delivers the resources, strong academic programs, and support our students truly deserve. Every family in Lynwood deserves equity because a quality education is a right, not a privilege. I know what it takes to right this ship, because I have done it before.
I am ready to listen, lead, and fight for every student in Lynwood. I humbly ask for your vote.

text: Age: 32
Occupation: Mother/Healthcare Advocate

As a lifelong resident of Lynwood and a proud parent raising my son within our community, I am deeply invested in the success of the Lynwood Unified School District. My family has personally benefited from the district's essential programs, which have provided me with the stability to balance my career as a single mother while my son thrives in his transitional kinder program.

I am running for the Board of Education because I believe every family in Lynwood deserves access to the same life-changing opportunities that have supported us. My priority is to protect and expand the funding for the vital programs that working parents depend on. I am committed to transparency, fiscal responsibility, and ensuring that our schools remain a safe, nurturing environment where every student can succeed.

With your vote, I will serve as a dedicated advocate for our children, our educators, and our families. Together, we can build a stronger, more supported future for all Lynwood students. I humbly ask for your vote to serve on the Lynwood Unified School District board.
